title: metastability
body:
**Metastability** is a [[Bi-stable elements|bi-stable element]] caught between its two
stable values, sitting at some intermediate [[Voltage]] that is neither a valid 0 nor a
valid 1. Balance a pencil on its point: it will fall, but you cannot say when or which way.

How you get there:

- An [[SR-Latch]] driven with $S=R=1$ and then released to $S=R=0$ at the same instant.
  Both halves try to win and neither does.
- A [[Flip-Flop]] whose data input changes too close to the clock edge, violating the
  setup or hold time.
- Any [[Asynchronous]] signal sampled by a [[Synchronous]] circuit, which is why crossing
  clock domains is a real engineering problem rather than a wiring problem.

The output eventually resolves to 0 or 1, but the resolution time is unbounded in theory,
and the downstream circuit may read the garbage value in the meantime. The standard
mitigation is a synchroniser: two [[Flip-Flop]]s in series, so the first one absorbs the
metastable event and the second sees a settled value.
